This dipole is $\mathord{\approx}10$ per cent below the finite-time value in the tested configurations. For oblate ejecta, the leading term is quadrupolar and is set by a single shape parameter. Effective models of 19 off-centre sub-Chandrasekhar explosions recover the MC peak times, peak luminosities, and width ratios to median errors of 3, 4, and 6 per cent, and the extent in $L_{\mathrm p}$ of the MC tracks, but underestimate the width-ratio variation with viewing angle by a factor of 2 to 3. An oblate construction captures the scale of peak luminosity variations in six equal-mass white-dwarf collisions. The model tracks remain inconsistent with the observed distribution, and for asymmetric models the transverse viewing-angle variation adds to the tension.

papers.title: Swept by the Galactic Tide: How Galactic Tides and Stellar Encounters Drive the Evolution of Wide Binaries and Their Giant Planets
papers.abstract: Wide stellar binaries ($a_b > 10^3$ AU) are common throughout the Galaxy, and many host extrasolar planets. Comparing planets in wide binaries with those around single stars can reveal whether a distant stellar companion affects planet formation. Such a comparison cannot be made directly, however: unlike in single-star systems, the Galactic tide and passing field stars dramatically reshape wide binaries over Gyr timescales, influencing the orbital properties and stability of the planets they host. In this work, we present N-body simulations demonstrating how the Galactic tide and stellar encounters sculpt the orbits of super-Jupiters on 1-6.5 AU orbits in wide binary systems on Sun-like Galactic orbits over 9 Gyr. We predict systematically higher orbital eccentricities for planets in wide binaries compared to single-star systems, with the most significant differences in older systems and those with more massive binary companions. Planetary ejections and disruptions are also common, and we find that planet-hosting binaries with orbits nearly perpendicular to the Galactic midplane are preferentially depleted. In our most optimistic estimate, the maximum hot Jupiter production rate is enhanced by up to a factor of ~3 relative to binaries without Galactic perturbations. A significant fraction of these binaries are also ionized (the stars become unbound), with a preference for ionization in lower-mass binaries, while the eccentricity distribution of survivors relaxes from mildly superthermal to nearly thermal. These results provide testable predictions for the population of giant planets in wide binaries soon to be revealed by Gaia DR4 and DR5.

papers.title: Magellan PFS Discovery of a Cold Gas Giant Exoplanet Likely Formed by a Gas Disk Gravitational Instability
papers.abstract: Using the Planet Finder Spectrograph (PFS) on the 6.5-m Magellan Clay Telescope at the Las Campanas Observatory we have discovered a cold gas giant exoplanet orbiting the K7V dwarf star HIP88962. 16 yrs of PFS observations imply an exoplanet with an orbital period of $\approx$ 19.3 yrs and a radial velocity semiamplitude (K) of 94.9 m s$^{-1}$. With a host star mass of 0.62 $M_\odot$, this implies a planet mass $M_p sin(i) \sim 5 M_{Jup}$. While stable M dwarfs have a PFS RMS of $\approx$ 3 m s$^{-1}$, the single Keplerian fit for HIP88962 has an RMS of $\approx$ 6 m s$^{-1}$, hinting at a second exoplanet. The best double planet Keplerian fit, with a 4.113 d period, still results in a RMS of $\approx$ 5 m s$^{-1}$. HIP88962 has Ca II H lines with twice the emission of four stable stars, implying that stellar activity may contribute to the RMS jitter error for the single Keplerian fit. When combined with Hipparcos and Gaia astrometry, HIP88962 b has a nearly edge-on orbit with inclination 91 $\pm$ 22 deg, true planet mass $4.83$ M$_{Jup}$, semimajor axis 6.15 $\pm$ 0.5 au, and eccentricity 0.718 $\pm$ 0.02. Including a PFS jitter of $\approx$ 7 m s$^{-1}$ yields $\chi^2 = 0.995$ for the combined solution. A massive gas giant orbiting at $\approx$ 6 au around a 0.62 $M_\odot$ star is incompatible with published core accretion population synthesis models, but consistent with formation by gas disk gravitational instability.

papers.title: Globular Clusters in the Time of JWST. II. Looks like the second, moves like the first: the syrphid-like intermediate population of NGC 2808
papers.abstract: The present-day kinematics of multiple populations in globular clusters can retain information about their initial conditions and can therefore help trace how the different populations formed. We combine JWST and HST photometry and proper motions to study the internal dynamics of four populations in NGC 2808 out to about eight half-light radii: the first population (1P) and three second-population groups with increasing light-element processing (2Pa, 2Pb, and 2Pc), providing the first detailed kinematic characterisation of the chemically intermediate 2Pa. We find significant kinematic differences between the populations. While all four have similar sky-projected radial velocity dispersions, 2Pb and 2Pc have lower tangential dispersions than 1P and are strongly radially anisotropic, whereas 2Pa shares the only mildly anisotropic kinematics of 1P. Therefore, chemically distinct 2P groups have different dynamical properties, suggesting that they formed under different conditions and/or experienced a different subsequent dynamical evolution. In the outer JWST field, the velocity dispersion depends only weakly on stellar mass, with hints of inverted equipartition. The difference between radial and tangential equipartition is similar for 1P and 2Pa and decreases towards 2Pc, a trend that remains tentative given the uncertainties. Our results show that 2P is not a dynamically homogeneous group, and that the kinematics of its individual groups provide a key constraint for multiple population formation scenarios.

papers.title: The origin of Potassium in Galactic chemical evolution - The effect of C-O shell mergers in massive stars
papers.abstract: The Galactic chemical evolution (GCE) of potassium (K) and of most other odd-Z elements remains poorly understood: models generally underproduce the observed [K/Fe] over a wide metallicity range, depending on the adopted massive star yields. A proposed site for efficient K nucleosynthesis is the merger between the oxygen and carbon shells (C-O shell merger) that can occur in massive stars a few hours before core collapse. Some GCE models with specific yield sets have been shown to reconcile predictions with observations. Here we re-analyse these yield sets to quantify the contribution of C-O shell mergers to K production and what the Galactic evolution of K implies about the occurrence of these events. We analyse 194 pre-supernova models from three independent yield sets, covering a wide range of initial masses, metallicities and rotational velocities, and including both single and binary-stripped stars. We identify the progenitors undergoing a C-O shell merger and compute GCE models with and without their contribution. In all three sets, the enhanced K production can be traced back to a small number of C-O merger progenitors, which eject up to ~10-50 times more K than non-merger progenitors of similar mass. Without them, no model reproduces the observations and [K/Fe] is sub-solar over most of the metallicity range. With them, [K/Fe] is enhanced only within the metallicity window where mergers occur in each grid. Binarity itself plays a minor role, as single stars alone produce similar amounts of K. Since the K synthesised in a C-O merger is essentially primary, the observed nearly linear increase of [K/H] with [Fe/H] can be reproduced only if C-O shell mergers occur with a similar frequency at all metallicities. K could therefore be used to infer the occurrence rate of C-O shell mergers in massive stars as a function of time.

papers.title: Radiation, Thermochemistry, and Stellar Feedback in DISPATCH
papers.abstract: The growth of massive stars depends on whether their accretion flows survive radiation and outflow feedback from the forming stellar population. We present an extension of DISPATCH that couples directional stellar radiation, diffuse infrared transport, and thermochemistry to self-gravitating magnetohydrodynamics, individual stellar accretion, and protostellar jets. This AMR-based method uses DISPATCH's local timestepping, allowing stellar environments and their larger scale cluster environments to step on separate timescales, and providing the framework needed to scale to long-duration simulations of GMCs. Direct radiation is transported in multiple bands, including both ionizing and nonionizing radiation, and uses short characteristics to maintain source directions and shadowing. Diffuse radiation is implemented for IR reprocessed light, with M1 and stationary ray options for transport. The thermochemical model includes atomic and molecular hydrogen and helium chemistry, and metal cooling and dust. It also includes a composition-dependent equation of state. Stellar masses grow through accretion of gas rather than a prescribed IMF, allowing stellar masses to respond to the evolving gas supply and feedback. In tests, multiple-source illumination retains geometric shadows while diffuse reprocessing heats shielded material, and tests of jets, ionization fronts, and radiation pressure demonstrate expected behavior and convergence. Ionization fronts also cross asynchronous refinement boundaries with late-time propagation speeds within a few percent of analytic predictions. Together, these developments provide a framework for determining how radiative and mechanical feedback modify the duration and efficiency of accretion from turbulent clouds, connecting the gas supply to individual stars with the high-mass stellar initial mass function.

papers.title: The full Gaia colour-magnitude diagram with white dwarfs reveals a declining Milky Way star formation history
papers.abstract: White dwarfs (WDs) provide a fossil record of the Milky Way star formation history (SFH) through the combined effects of stellar evolution and cooling. They have, however, generally been modelled in isolation from the non-degenerate population, so that no single self-consistent set of Galactic assumptions has been required to reproduce both. We present CALOMERA, a semi-analytic chemo-dynamical population synthesis framework in which the vertical density profiles of mono-age subpopulations are computed self-consistently with the Galactic potential and coupled to modern WD cooling sequences, metallicity-dependent progenitor lifetimes and synthetic photometry. We calibrate 18 parameters describing the initial mass function, SFH, initial-final mass relation and WD population against a Gaia DR3 sample of $7.98\times10^{6}$ stars within 1 kpc, including $1.1\times10^{5}$ WDs. The calibrated model reproduces the star counts in each colour-magnitude diagram region to within 3% and the total number count to within 0.5%, compared with the 81% excess in the predicted WD count obtained with the previous main-sequence-only calibration. The recovered SFH peaks early, declines exponentially thereafter, and includes two recent bursts, located at $\tau\approx2.4$ and $0.5$ Gyr. Three cooling libraries (Montr\'{e}al, BaSTI and LPCODE) yield comparably good fits, with differences confined to ${\rm M_G}\gtrsim15$ mag. The predicted luminosity function is in reasonable agreement with the 100 pc Gaia WD sample. We further predict the Galactic WD distribution and differential number counts for surveys of varying depth. Extending the framework to the substellar regime using ATMO models, we predict the Galactic L, T, and Y dwarf populations and their contribution to the deep JWST fields.
